content:
Good puzzle, but it needs more test cases. It would be good to implement these scenarios:
- Lots of dictionary words
- Lots of players (you might choose to remove the names and give each player a number so you don't have to think of names)
- Long dictionary words (even if it's more letters than a scrabble game would allow)
- Dictionary words that are longer than any player's tile amount, but that only contain letters that are in a player's hand
- Players' tile counts are greater than the length of some or all dictionary words
- Every player has the exact same letters and there is a matching dictionary word
- No player has a matching dictionary word (You would have to state whether that should mean everyone ties or a loss is called)

For these ones you would have to remove the 'exact anagram' part of the goal but I think it would be cool.
- A player's hand contains all the pieces of the best word, plus extra. That player wins.
- 2 players' hands can make the best dictionary word, but one of those players has extra letters. Ideally the extra letters are contained in the best word. Those 2 players tie.

Input
* Please include the variable type in each description and revise the section as follows:

<<Line 1>>: A string [[mode]], representing the game mode, which is either {{high}} or {{low}}.
<<Line 2>>: An integer [[n]] for the number of players.
<<Next [[n]] lines>>: Two space-separated strings [[name]] and [[hand]], representing a player's name and the letter tiles in their hand.
<<Next line>>: An integer [[d]] for the number of words in the dictionary.
<<Next [[d]] lines>>: A string [[word]] for a word in the dictionary.

Output
* Please rewrite this section as follows:

<<1 or more lines>>: The winners' names and their winning words, separated by a space, with one winner per line.

Constraints
* Please replace "each hand/word" with "[[name]], [[hand]], [[word]]".

* Please remove the constraint on mode.

* Please replace the final two constraints with these two:

[[name]]s and [[word]]s are unique in each case.
[[name]], [[hand]] and [[word]] consist of lowercase English letters only.

* The upper bounds may be revised later, subject to further review.

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement, e.g. write answer, or write winner word.

Difficulty
* Please set the difficulty to Easy.

Cover picture
* Please add a cover picture for the puzzle.

Cases
* To be reviewed.

Thanks.

* You need to include the scrabble tile values.

* Validators need to pair with tests

* The description has some unnecessary steps. The program does not use *every* anagram, only the first alphabetically.
I think this contribution may can set to Ready.
Hope scrabble doesnt rule this out. I added my twist.

There's indeed some overlap with the existing Scrabble puzzle https://www.codingame.com/training/medium/scrabble . For the record, the main differences at present (on 23 August 2026) are:

* The original puzzle doesn't require a word to use all the available tiles in the hand, whereas your puzzle requires an exact match of the letters in the hand (anagram matching).

* Your puzzle requires evaluating several hands (groups of scrambled letters), whereas the original puzzle requires evaluating only one hand.

* Your puzzle has high and low modes, whereas the original puzzle always selects the word with the highest score.

* The original puzzle uses the first appearance in the dictionary as its tie-breaker, whereas your puzzle uses alphabetical order.

* The upper bound on the number of words in the dictionary is much smaller in your puzzle.

The first four points will require some rewriting of the solution to the existing puzzle to address this one. The first point, in particular, will simplify the matching logic a lot.
